# `⌸` — Key

Monadic operator. Keys: `Alt-q =`. Hanzi: `组` (`組`)

`K f⌸Y` groups major cells of `Y` by corresponding keys in `K`. Calls `key f group`; groups appear in first-occurrence order.

```bpl
1 1 2{+/⍵}⌸10 20 30 ⍝ 30 30
```

`f⌸Y` uses `Y` as keys and their positions as values.

Keys match with [tolerance](../evaluation.qmd#equality-and-ordering), as in `≠`. Results assemble with fill. Empty input calls `f` once for its prototype.

## How Key runs

Key calls `f` once on all its groups where it can, whatever `f`'s spelling, as a [map](../evaluation.qmd#functions-and-effects) calls its operand once on all its cells. A fold or scan of each group of a vector, such as `K (+/⊢)⌸Y` or `K {+/⍵}⌸Y`, reads each item of `Y` by its group's number. [`•explain`](../system/explain.qmd) reports that route as `"key classes"`.

```bpl
1 1 2(+/⊢)⌸10 20 30                            ⍝ 30 30
e←•explain "1 1 2{+/⍵}⌸10 20 30"
[(⊂"key classes")∊e.routes.route ; (⊂"batching")∊e.fast.rule]  ⍝ [$t $t]
```
